leads.question: On a public HyperEVM replica that serves debug_traceBlockByNumber (nanoreth f0cad31 or b92ad36, which reproduce the producer's receipts roots), how often did the closed producer execute, in the newest 50,000 validated blocks and in any contract, the operand shapes the PoolManager needs: MULMOD with a product of 2^256 or more and a modulus of three or four limbs (FullMath.sol:48), MULMOD with modulus 2^256-1 (FullMath.sol:24), DIV of a 512 bit remainder shape, SAR of a negative word, SIGNEXTEND from bytes 3 to 30 with the sign bit set, BYTE, shifts by 256 or more, KECCAK256 of 64 bytes and overlapping MCOPY? Report the shapes with zero executions.
leads.why: This transfers the MegaETH producer census of cycles 33 and 35 to HyperEVM. eth_call equality on the official endpoint does not show what the producer runs. A shape the producer has never executed is one that an ordinary account could reach first with a pool it creates, and a wrong producer result there would change a swap amount paid out of the PoolManager. The census shrinks that set to what no mined transaction has covered.

leads.question: Run the last compiled PoolManager block that OPCODES.md lists as not run whole from the shipped gcc 15.2.0 build (the delta read in clear, src/PoolManager.sol:310-319 with CurrencyDelta.getDelta at src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:18-23) on logged real states, with the delta positive, zero, negative and equal to the amount, and compare the TLOAD result, the comparison at :314 and the delta written by _accountDelta with the interpreter.
leads.why: Monad validators run the compiled code while eth_call runs the interpreter, so this block is the only PoolManager code path any account can call that has not run whole on the code that sets Monad state. clear is unpermissioned and changes a delta without a transfer.

leads.question: Run the journal machine code of celo-reth v1.0.10 (sload, sstore, tstore, checkpoint, checkpoint_commit, checkpoint_revert and JournalEntry::revert, which the Celo binary names at 0x1e90200, 0x1e91150, 0x1d66aa0, 0x1d61dd0 and 0x4fb8c20) and the matching routines of xlayer-reth v0.0.7.3-rc.1 through rethj.py with 2,000 nested-frame sequences each over the Lock, NonzeroDeltaCount, CurrencyReserves, CurrencyDelta and pool slots, with the restore-zero and skipped-entry faults planted. Do the transient words and pool words after each inner revert equal pyevm.py?
leads.why: This consolidates the two duplicate cycle 36 leads. The two builds share no journal function with any lifted build, and a revert that kept a transient credit while the token transfer rolled back would let a caller exit unlock with an unpaid delta (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114).

leads.question: Run the journal routines of arc-execution v0.8.6 (SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD, TSTORE, checkpoint, checkpoint_revert) through rethj.py, and for a value CALL that check_blocklist_and_create_log rejects (crates/evm/src/evm.rs lines 516-605 at v0.8.6) inside a frame that later reverts, do the PoolManager's transient words, the native balances and the emitted Transfer log match the revm journal rules?
leads.why: Arc's native USDC moves through a frame hook outside the instruction handlers, and its order against the checkpoint was not found in the stripped binary. A native credit in settle (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354) that survived a rolled back value move would be a credit without payment.

leads.question: Run cycles/036/arbitrum-family.work/scripts/provevec.py (30,222 vectors: SHL, SHR and SAR for every count 0 to 320 and counts near 2^32, 2^64, 2^128 and 2^255, every BYTE index and SIGNEXTEND width, divisions and modular operations by divisors of one to four limbs) on bsc-rpc.publicnode.com (reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix, ruint 1.18.0), rpc.xlayer.tech (ruint 1.18.0) and mainnet.megaeth.com (ruint 1.19.0), each batch bracketed by web3_clientVersion. Do any differ?
leads.why: The vectors were built for the Arbitrum family only. The op-stack-custom-gas verifier found that ruint 1.18.0 predates the shift and byte() fixes of PR 603 and ran only 242 such cases on two endpoints; reth-bsc and MegaETH were not included.

leads.question: What does ruint PR 603 change? Read the ruint CHANGELOG.md and src/bits.rs at the 1.18.0 and 1.20.0 tags on raw.githubusercontent.com, and find whether the revm 35.0.1 and 37.0.3 SHL, SHR, SAR and BYTE handlers bound the shift amount or index to below 256 before calling overflowing_shl, overflowing_shr, checked_shl or byte().
leads.why: op-stack-custom-gas says PR 603 fixes u32 casts in the wrapping shift fast paths, and its verifier read the changelog as overflow-flag false negatives in overflowing_shl, overflowing_shr and byte(). The two units contradict each other, and the clearance for the ruint 1.18.0 builds depends on which is right.

leads.question: On the five networks whose native asset has a token face, list every way native value can reach the PoolManager without a call to settle (forced sends from a SELFDESTRUCT in the creating transaction, bridge and CCTP deliveries, system mints, fee or reward credits), and for each, can an account other than the payer run it between its own sync(face) and settle in one transaction?
leads.why: src/PoolManager.sol:349-364 credits the rise in the face balance to whoever settles, and the face balance is the native balance. The cycle 35 table covers bridge relays (F-137) and forced native value, but its fee, reward and system rows rest on reading only. A path that a third party pays and an attacker books would take value from the pools of either currency id.
